quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to its frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlight at all times. Wear bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly. These steps help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater get in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Riding faster is dangerous because they may tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: There is no need to do a head check if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors provide a full view of the road around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can assume drivers will properly respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What happens with long-term exposure to wind noise?

options.text: It is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these regulatory signs.

questions.question: How often should you completely check your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator improve their visibility?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing to be seen better. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What happens when you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is acceptable as long as no vehicles are near you.
You can end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may lose control and end up in another lane or off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, which of the following should you NOT check?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shininess
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check how shiny they are.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen by other drivers.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Which fabric protects motorcycle riders best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What helps reduce head and neck injuries in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to prevent head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Crashes happen most often to:

options.text: Those who know their motorcycle well.
Those who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who have not had training and do not know their motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration in hot weather.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the important thing is to see the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: You should not ride directly beside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use that lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside a vehicle is dangerous because the driver cannot see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after having one drink:

options.text: Guarantees you will not be arrested for drinking and riding.
Guarantees your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average. The time needed varies, so it is safest to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap is not considered protective gear.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Do not matter much since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no vehicles are near you.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are in danger, so use your turn signals to tell others your plans. Always use them when you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It can greatly reduce the risk of serious head injury.
It makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can greatly reduce the risk of serious head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly reduces your chance of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: What is the correct way to pass a vehicle?

options.text: You may go over the speed limit until you finish passing.
You may ignore "No passing zone" markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and only pass in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and only pass in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction for motorcycles. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are more hazardous than dry pavement.
